classification.difficultyReason: Use the five-minute hint to track the hour hand and justify the supplied clock separation.

content.prompt:
The angle between the two hands of a clock at 9:35 a.m. is $77.5^\circ$.

Explain why. (hint: how much does the hour hand move in 5 minutes?)

spec.sourceRegion: Question 18, clock beneath the stem at left
spec.description: An unnumbered circular clock has twelve inward hour ticks, a black centre point, two red arrowed hands and an unlabelled smaller-angle arc. The minute hand points towards 7; the shorter hour hand points between 9 and 10.
spec.mathematics: At 9:35, clockwise positions from 12 are 210 degrees for the minute hand and 287.5 degrees for the hour hand. Their smaller separation is 77.5 degrees. These values determine the geometry but are not printed on the diagram.
spec.answerVisibility: Retain the supplied hands and unlabelled angle arc. Do not add angle values or clock numerals.

answer.short: The hands are $210^\circ$ and $287.5^\circ$ clockwise from 12, so the smaller angle is $287.5^\circ-210^\circ=77.5^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The hour hand moves $30^\circ$ in 60 minutes, hence $2.5^\circ$ in 5 minutes.

Measured clockwise from 12, the minute-hand position is
$$\begin{align*}180^\circ+30^\circ&=210^\circ.\end{align*}$$

There are seven 5-minute intervals in 35 minutes, so the hour-hand position is
$$\begin{align*}270^\circ+7\times2.5^\circ&=287.5^\circ.\end{align*}$$

The smaller angle between the hands is
$$\begin{align*}287.5^\circ-210^\circ&=77.5^\circ.\end{align*}$$
